acceptance_evidence: Nine useful partial workflows and the retained inherently manual migration strategy. Literal mode/flags, bounded supplied counts and positive typed links prepare review but cannot establish global protection, origin exclusivity, operational DDoS/log coverage, policy enforcement, route preference, maintained failover or demand. No whole predicate is defensible for these ten recommendations from the permitted inputs alone.
supported_modes: AzureRM 4.50.0 raw Terraform with supplied module snapshots and optional plan; reviewed ARM 2024-02-01 Front Door and 2024-05-01 Network plus 2021-05-01-preview diagnostics; existing no-restore Bicep; saved normalized resources and injected scoped details. Policy context uses the existing bounded saved policy-export/injected metadata path only, not new policy evaluation or IaC policy interpretation. Missing or sensitive facts stay unknown.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit Front Door WAF mode/state/SKU and supplied managed/custom rule counts, typed WAF association and domain/endpoint IDs with an explicit all-path marker.
evidence_requirements: Reconcile every exposed domain, endpoint, route, origin and region with actual policy attachment and scope precedence; the reviewed 2024 schema does not represent newer profile/route scope semantics.

Review explicit enabled Prevention versus Detection, rule actions, custom Allow short-circuiting, rule versions, exclusions and Standard versus Premium capabilities. Counts or SKU alone never establish blocking protection.
Reviewer decision: does attributable original-time path and operational evidence establish the intended global inbound HTTP/S protection without bypass? Keep outcome blank until supplied.
recommendations.limitations: Bounded configured attachments and flags are not actual requests, health, effective WAF actions or complete region/path coverage. Classic Front Door and newer unsupported APIs remain unsupported, not silently converted.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit gateway/WAF/subnet links and minimized FDID custom-condition shapes alongside source-tag/port rule summaries.
evidence_requirements: For public origins verify both AzureFrontDoor.Backend filtering and rejection of absent/wrong X-Azure-FDID for the exact intended profile; a header rule candidate alone or a shared service tag is insufficient.

Reconcile effective NSG priorities, protocols, source/destination/port coverage, required management traffic and gateway/listener/path WAF policies. Withheld header values must be checked using redacted external evidence.
Reviewer decision: are all alternate origin endpoints blocked, including public bypass when Private Link is used, with attributable exclusivity evidence?
recommendations.limitations: No rule interpreter, packet test, DNS/health request or actual header value is retained. A literal condition/action summary is not exact-profile validation or effective origin lockdown.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit gateway subnet placement, WAF reference and bounded configured backend entry counts without hosts or addresses.
evidence_requirements: Bind the proxy subnets and all real backends to the approved workload landing-zone/VNet ownership and exposure model. Configured names, entry counts or one subnet do not establish co-location.
Reconcile service-specific placement, DNS/TLS, actual routes, shared-versus-workload responsibility and health independently; Front Door itself is global, not deployed into a workload VNet.
Reviewer decision: is required reverse-proxy placement workload-aligned with attributable actual backend and ownership evidence?
recommendations.limitations: Backend hosts and private addresses are withheld. Supplied entries are not distinct instances, complete membership, health or accepted workload architecture.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit per-public-IP DDoS mode/plan and positive IP-configuration relationships alongside existing VNet plan context.
evidence_requirements: Inventory every supported public endpoint and resolve IP Protection versus NetworkInherited protection to the actual protected VNet/plan and attached service.

Reconcile supported endpoint/SKU/region constraints and exclusions: the reviewed architecture excludes NAT Gateway and Virtual WAN; platform Front Door protection is not protection of an exposed origin.
Reviewer decision: does original-time coverage and operational mitigation evidence cover every applicable application/platform public endpoint?
recommendations.limitations: Configured mode and positive references are not effective mitigation or full-population coverage. No plan lookup, traffic probe, attack simulation or new Azure read occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Retained manual outbound migration strategy with explicit defaultOutboundAccess, NAT/route associations and versioned current-versus-frozen retirement findings.
evidence_requirements: The frozen checklist says September 30, 2025; inspected Learn revision e8c3f408 instead describes APIs released after March 31, 2026 for new VNets, earlier-API behavior and unchanged existing VNets. The dynamic announcement shell did not expose its timeline. Preserve both findings, never assert blanket shutdown.

Document accountable migration owner, affected existing/new/API/delegated-subnet populations, explicit NAT/LB/firewall egress paths, dependencies, Internet-next-hop exceptions, SNAT demand, rollback and maintenance/stop-deallocation requirements without executing them.

Reviewer decision: is the explicit outbound strategy and migration plan approved and backed by attributable dependency/path evidence? A private flag or NAT reference does not establish a plan or connectivity.
recommendations.limitations: An approved business migration strategy is inherently manual. No owner approval, VM stop, route change, deployment or egress test is fabricated; the original recommendation and manual disposition remain intact.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit three-category DDoS log configuration and typed workspace/storage destination with exact diagnostic target binding.
evidence_requirements: Resolve each setting's exact protected public-IP target and explicit DDoSProtectionNotifications, DDoSMitigationFlowLogs and DDoSMitigationReports enabled values; metrics-only, wrong targets or missing arrays do not establish logs.

Reconcile category groups, alternative Event Hub destinations, retention/access, routing and every protected-IP population. Unsupported or missing destination details remain unknown rather than absent.
Reviewer decision: are DDoS logs configured for all applicable protected IPs and demonstrably arriving/retained at the approved destination with original-time evidence?
recommendations.limitations: Per-setting category flags or built-in compliance are not ingestion or all-IP coverage. Event Hub destination interpretation and actual log reads remain outside this implementation.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Existing minimized saved assignment/exemption context, exact source-backed NIC policy identity and bounded positive VM/NIC/public-IP relationships in review preparation.
evidence_requirements: Pinned corp includes Deny-Public-IP-On-NIC, built-in 83a86a26-fd1f-447c-b59d-e51f44264114 version 1.0.0 with fixed deny and NIC-array alias logic. Distinguish it from deny-all-public-IP resource creation and from display-name matches.

Reconcile actual assignments at inherited/applicable scopes, definition versions, Default versus DoNotEnforce, selectors, overrides and exact notScopes/exemptions, expiry and approved exception evidence. Saved context hashes alone cannot decide effect or enforcement.
Reviewer decision: does attributable actual policy/evaluation and exception evidence establish the intended VM/NIC attachment governance without uncovered scopes or fabricated exclusions?
recommendations.limitations: Existing saved policy metadata intentionally withholds raw parameters and effective logic. Crosswalk associations remain unchanged; no new policy mapping/pass, policy trigger, remediation or permission change occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit connection kinds, typed gateway/circuit/local-gateway links, BGP/active-active flags and gateway subnet context.
evidence_requirements: Resolve actual ExpressRoute and S2S connections to the same intended network/site topology, supported coexistence/gateway/subnet constraints and independent failure domains.

Review both-direction steady-state route preference, equal versus more-specific prefixes, backup maintenance and actual failover/recovery evidence. S2S backup is not recommended for latency-sensitive, mission-critical or bandwidth-intensive workloads.
Reviewer decision: is primary ExpressRoute/backup VPN appropriate and demonstrably maintained for the actual workload, or is a documented multi-site ExpressRoute design required?
recommendations.limitations: Two resource kinds or activeActive=true cannot establish supported topology, route preference, health or resilient failover. No tunnel/route/traffic query occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Strict explicit routing weight 0..32000 and BGP flags bound to typed circuit/gateway references.
evidence_requirements: Identify every applicable circuit/site/prefix and intended direction, then reconcile on-premises local preference, communities, AS PATH and Azure connection weight using attributable saved configuration/route evidence.

Weight is considered before AS-path length for Azure outbound, not a generic customer local-preference setting. Microsoft peering removes private ASNs and does not honor arbitrary received communities; prefix specificity and asymmetry still matter.
Reviewer decision: does actual route/path evidence establish optimized preference in both directions and under failures? No arbitrary minimum weight or default of 10 is a compliance predicate.
recommendations.limitations: Weight/BGP configuration never proves the winning route or latency. Peer addresses, router labels, full route tables and secrets are withheld; no BGP/effective-route query or router change occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit reviewed gateway SKU, generation and kind alongside topology context, without numeric demand or throughput inference.
evidence_requirements: Bind SKU/generation to actual workload bandwidth, packets/flows, latency, tunnel/P2S mix, cipher, circuit capacity, growth, region availability and resilience objectives.

Current ExpressRoute scalable SKU is not supported by pinned AzureRM 4.50.0; unknown SKU/casing remains unknown. Published throughput is estimated/benchmark, not guaranteed; maintenance and private endpoints can reduce capacity.
Reviewer decision: does measured original-time demand and accepted capacity/failure headroom justify the supported selected SKU and current migration status?
recommendations.limitations: SKU/count/active-active does not establish bandwidth demand, SLA, measured throughput or appropriate sizing. No benchmark, billing read, deployment or gateway migration occurs.
